clue.text: Trendy sultry Romeo's stripped

indicators.note: Romeo is stripped, i.e. taken away from the word for sultry

parts.note: sultry weather is hot and humid, i.e. tropical
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fashionable, steamy Romeo has taken his clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' looks like undressing but signals removing R (Romeo) from TROPICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical is of current interest, so it is fashionable or trendy at the moment.

clue.text: I'm struggling with old play for London venue

indicators.note: struggling suggests things thrashing about, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: old is abbreviated to O, and play is taken as written, together supplying five letters of the mix

explanation.surface: An actor says he is having trouble with a dated play in a London theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia is a large exhibition hall in West London, used for shows and events.

clue.text: Unlimited rich ore that filled ancient vessels

indicators.note: without limits, so the outer letters of the phrase are dropped and the inner run is kept

explanation.surface: Rich ore once filled old ships' holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' are veins, not ships: the fluid ran in the bodies of the ancient gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this ethereal fluid flowed in place of blood in the veins of the gods.

clue.text: Plug English in top universities

indicators.note: in places the advert and English inside the word for top

parts.note: the acme is the top or peak
a plug is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: Advertise English at the best universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the world of higher learning and scholarship, embodied by universities collectively.

clue.text: CID managed with help from ambiguous source

indicators.note: managed here means handled or worked over, so the letters of CID and help are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The police detectives' department solved a case with a tip-off of doubtful origin.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force; 'managed' rearranges CID with HELP.
explanation.definitionFit: The oracle at Delphi gave famously two-edged answers, so Delphic describes utterances that are obscure or ambiguous, as from that source.

clue.text: Possible result of congress organised by Rome

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters of by Rome are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A political assembly arranged by Rome might produce something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'congress' is sexual intercourse, not a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is the early stage of offspring that can follow sexual union.

clue.text: Contested area in case pamphleteer comes round

indicators.note: the pamphleteer surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Thomas Paine wrote the pamphlet Common Sense
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: A disputed territory, just in case the political writer visits.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Paine was the radical eighteenth-century author of Common Sense; 'comes round' wraps his name round the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Palestine is a land whose sovereignty and borders remain disputed, a territory claimed by more than one party.

clue.text: Disturb cow in roundabout with no hesitation

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the hesitation sound is removed

parts.note: Ermintrude is the cow in the children's TV series The Magic Roundabout
erm is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone disrupts a cow on a traffic island without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Roundabout was a children's television show; its cow was Ermintrude. 'with no' removes ERM from her name.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to butt in where unwelcome, thereby disturbing or interrupting others.

clue.text: Forget about plump female in new very big play

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for forget is read backwards

parts.note: to omit is to forget or leave out

indicators.note: in puts the plump female inside the letters for very big

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very big
fat means plump
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Disregard the overweight woman in the huge new production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the word for forget, and 'in' places the plump female inside OS, the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens is a Shakespeare tragedy about a generous Athenian turned misanthrope.

clue.text: This writer's article abridged an old wives' tale

parts.note: the setter referring to themselves: belonging to this writer is my

indicators.note: abridged means cut short, so the article loses its final letter

parts.note: the definite article is the

explanation.surface: The writer's piece was cut down into a folk tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' shortens THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: An old wives' tale is a widely believed falsehood or traditional story, which is what a myth is.

clue.text: Back plan to expand talent and charm

indicators.note: the word for talent is made bigger by having the other piece put inside it

parts.note: talent is ability

indicators.note: Back tells us to read the word for plan from right to left

parts.note: an aim is a plan or intention

explanation.surface: Support a scheme to develop someone's gifts and attractiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the word for plan around, and 'to expand' sets it inside the talent word, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiability is friendly pleasantness, a close synonym of charm in the sense of agreeable manner.

clue.text: Euphorbia's left out of ostentatious display

definitions.note: the clue's 's is 'is', linking the plant name to the wordplay

indicators.note: left is taken out of the word for showy display

parts.note: a splurge is an extravagant, showy display or spending spree

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that the plant has been omitted from a showy flower display.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia is the botanical genus name for the plants commonly called spurges.

clue.text: Old Latin god saved unknown vessel for Greek traveller

indicators.note: the god holds and keeps the other letters inside him

parts.note: deus is the Latin word for god
in algebra y is an unknown quantity
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman deity rescued a mysterious ship carrying a Greek voyager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saved' puts the unknown and the vessel inside the Latin god; Y is the algebra convention for an unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus, hero of Homer's Odyssey, spent ten years wandering home from Troy, the archetypal Greek voyager.

clue.text: French region's ageless tongue and revolutionary law

definitions.note: the clue's 's is 'is', linking the region to the wordplay

indicators.note: ageless here means with the letters a-g-e removed

parts.note: a tongue is a language

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for law is read backwards

parts.note: a code is a body of law, as in the Code Napoleon

explanation.surface: A French region's timeless language and radical legal system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ageless' takes AGE out of LANGUAGE, leaving LANGU; 'revolutionary' turns CODE into EDOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Languedoc is a historic area of southern France, named after its Occitan speech, the langue d'oc.

clue.text: Aegean islands perhaps make meandering patterns

parts.note: the Aegean is a Greek sea, so Aegean things are Greek
keys are low islands, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: Islands in the Aegean could form winding shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags that the islands of the Aegean are only fancifully called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek key, or meander, is a decorative border of interlocking right-angled lines.

clue.text: Trees defining boundary of the Roman Empire

definitions.meaning: the Latin word ... was the fortified frontier of the Roman Empire

explanation.surface: Lines of trees marked the edge of ancient Rome's territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a Latin word, pronounced as two syllables, used by historians for frontiers such as Hadrian's Wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Lime trees and the Roman limes, its fortified frontier, share this spelling though they are different words.

clue.text: She oversaw agriculture before entering civil service

indicators.note: the word for before goes into the abbreviation for civil service

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A woman ran farming policy before joining the civil service.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a minister's career; the definition is the Roman goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceres was the Roman goddess of agriculture, grain and harvests, giving us the word cereal.

clue.text: Roundabout very like one seen during the day before

indicators.note: the other pieces are found within the word for the day before

parts.note: eve is the day before an event
as means like
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traffic circle looks very like one spotted the previous day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen during' places the three short pieces inside the word for the day before. 'Roundabout' looks like the traffic circle but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An evasive answer is indirect, circling the point rather than meeting it, just as a roundabout reply does.

clue.text: Leave Scottish woman running temple

parts.note: to part is to leave or depart
hen is a Scottish term of address for a woman
a machine that is on is running

explanation.surface: A Scotswoman leaves the place of worship, still jogging.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon on the Athens Acropolis is the famous temple to the goddess Athena.

clue.text: Stupendous upstanding citizen wins one bronze

indicators.note: wins means takes in or gains, so the reversed citizen holds the other pieces
in a down entry upstanding means written upwards, i.e. reversed

parts.note: cit is a short form of citizen
I is the Roman numeral for one
tan is a bronze colour

explanation.surface: A remarkable, upright citizen takes a bronze medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' reverses the short form of citizen, giving TIC, and 'wins' takes ITAN in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means colossal or enormous in scale, like the giant Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Ring about scenery put up for Euripides drama

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: in a down entry put up means written upwards, so the word for scenery is reversed

parts.note: theatre scenery is the sets

explanation.surface: Phone someone about scenery built for a Greek tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns SETS into STES.
explanation.definitionFit: Orestes is a tragedy by Euripides about Agamemnon's son after he kills his mother.

clue.text: Probes go round it and go under it

indicators.note: in a down entry under means placed below, so the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a go is a turn

explanation.surface: Space probes orbit something and pass beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'it' is sex appeal, SA, with TURN (go) placed under it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringed planet has been orbited by space probes such as Cassini.

clue.text: Consequence of impact made by old ship's cat?

definitions.text: Consequence of impact made by old ship's cat?

parts.words: Consequence of impact made by old ship's cat?
parts.note: the cat o' nine tails, a whip used on old sailing ships, leaves a stroke across a sailor's spine; read the other way, the word is a recoil or adverse reaction

explanation.surface: A sailor asks what a ship's cat leaves behind when it strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship's cat is not a pet but the cat o' nine tails, the naval whip; its flogging struck the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong adverse reaction to an event is a recoil caused by it, and literally a whipping stroke on the spine.

clue.text: Not quite the perfect ancient city

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the perfect choice is the best

explanation.surface: Something falls just short of ideal, like a ruined old metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the final T from BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a major city of ancient Greece, and also the name of a great capital of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: River rises, overwhelming grand Scottish town

indicators.note: overwhelming means engulfing, so the reversed river surrounds the other letter
in a down entry rises means going upwards, so the river name is reversed

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river
G abbreviates grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A river in flood engulfs a fine Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns NILE into ELIN, and 'overwhelming' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a town in Moray in northeast Scotland, famous for its ruined cathedral.

clue.text: Essential function shortly to entertain queen

indicators.note: entertain means to hold as a guest, so the queen goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
anon is an old word meaning shortly or soon

explanation.surface: A vital role soon hosts the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to entertain' lodges the queen abbreviation between the function and the word for shortly; the answer is a Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, literally 'without which not', names an indispensable condition, something essential.

clue.text: Bought horse, one clad in black

parts.note: got can mean obtained or bought
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: Someone purchased a horse, a black-clothed rider.
explanation.walkthrough: H for horse comes via heroin: both are slang names for the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Goths are a subculture known for dressing in black clothes and dark make-up.

clue.text: Jam in a city in Italy

parts.note: to be in a jam is to be in a mess

explanation.surface: Stuck in a traffic jam in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Messina is the port city in Sicily, part of Italy, facing the mainland across the strait named after it.

clue.text: Former chemical business head's hostility

parts.note: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a British chemicals firm now defunct
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: An old chemical company's boss shows antagonism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' here is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours such as Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Iciness is coldness of manner, an unfriendly frostiness close to hostility.
